articles.title: In 2015, Tiger Woods invested in Full Swing, a golf-simulator maker; in July 2026 Versant agreed to buy it for $530 million, and his reported 2% stake could be worth up to $10.6 million
articles.summary: In an impressive financial move, Tiger Woods' stake in Full Swing, which he invested in back in 2015, could be worth over $10 million following the company's acquisition by Versant Media Group for $530 million. Discover the growth of golf simulators and their impact on the game.
articles.body: Tiger Woods invested in the golf simulator manufacturer Full Swing in 2015. On July 6, 2026, Versant Media Group agreed to acquire the company for $530 million, subject to customary adjustments, according to its Form 8-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. As per Front Office Sports, Woods owns shares worth 1% to 2%. Considering that a 2% share would amount to around $10.6 million at the valuation price, it is clear that this figure is just an approximation.Versant announced the complete purchase of Full Swing on August 3, 2026Versant’s Media Group’s press release names Bruin Capital, the majority owner and a group of minority investors as the sellers. Bruin paid $160 million for Full Swing in 2021, as Front Office Sports noted, so the $530 million sale is roughly three times that figure five years later. Versant, having spun off from Comcast and owning Golf Channel, made this announcement on August 3, 2026. Its second-quarter results, filed on August 6, also list the acquisition as completed after the quarter ended.Wood’s stake is an estimate based on one unnamed sourceWoods has been Full Swing brand ambassador since 2015 and Front Office Sports says he has had a significant influence on the company's business direction and product development despite holding a minority stake. Since his stake could be as low as 1%, the $10.6 million is a ceiling rather than a confirmed payout and the final figure could shift with purchase price adjustments and profit-sharing terms. He has had a significant influence on the companies' business direction and product development despite holding a minority stake. Full Swing is the official licensed simulator of the PGA Tour and a technology partner of TGL, the indoor golf league co-founded by Woods and Rory McIlroy. Jordan Spieth and Xander Schauffele are among the athletes associated with the brand.Simulator users grew from 3.8 million in 2015 to 8.1 million in 2024Woods backed Full Swing in 2015; the same year, the National Golf Foundation counted 3,800,000 simulator and screen golf users, according to its 2025 white paper, The Golf Simulator Opportunity. It puts the 2024 figure at 8.1 million. The National Golf Foundation’s 2025 report also found that 51% of golf simulator users had not played on a traditional golf course in the previous 12 months, up from 42% a decade earlier. The foundation Research also found that three-quarters of simulator users were likely to return.Golfers listed various reasons why they chose to play indoors. Weather-proofing was mentioned by 59% of golfers and performance improvement by 43%, while 34% mentioned performance analysis.The National Golf Foundation’s study puts US golf participation at a record 47.2 million in 2024, which counts formats like simulators on top of the 28.1 million who played on a course. The study is based on two surveys conducted in November and December 2024. One survey of 354 US golf venues and another one of 569 core golfers, who played at least eight rounds in the past year.70% of facilities with simulators report a positive financial impactAs noted above in the NGF report, 70% of facilities with simulators have recorded positive financial effects. According to the same research, 80% of those facilities reached profitability within a year of getting a simulator and 44% saw a positive financial impact within the first month, rather than a full return on the investment. Operators spent an average of $45,000 per bay. Each session cost an average of $55, while customers spent an additional $40 on food and drinks. 6.5% of all US golf facilities had installed simulators at the time of the survey, while another 13% were planning to get simulators in 1 to 2 years. Of those not having simulators, 72% stated space was their constraint and 53% pointed out the cost.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Defiant DeChambeau 'grateful' for LIV, vague on future plans
articles.summary: Bryson DeChambeau said on Sunday he does not regret joining LIV Golf and offered no new details of his future plans in his first public comments since the di...
articles.body:
Bryson DeChambeau said on Sunday he does not regret joining LIV Golf and offered no new details of his future plans in his first public comments since the divisive tour announced it is shutting down.

DeChambeau was arguably the highest profile member of a swathe of golf stars who defected from the traditional PGA Tour to free-spending LIV in 2022, turning the golf world on its head.

The two-time US Open winner had continued to staunchly defend the rebel tour even after its Saudi backers pulled the plug this year, expressing optimism for a now-aborted "LIV 2.0" relaunch plan even as others like Jon Rahm jumped ship.

With LIV announcing on Thursday that it will shutter for good, DeChambeau issued a statement expressing gratitude for his experience with the rebel tour.

"I'm not going to rewrite the last four years. I made a decision I believed in, and I'm grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home," he said.

"The record crowds in Adelaide and Johannesburg will stick with me for the rest of my life.

"I believed this game could reach more people, in more places, in a new way. I still believe that. And I gave it everything I had to keep team golf alive."

DeChambeau expressed confidence that LIV Golf's distinctive team-based format would be successful in the future.

"I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it's essential to growing the game," he said.

Several former LIV stars have announced they will play on the DP World (European) Tour next season -- a potential route to one day returning to the US PGA Tour.

DeChambeau, whose personal commercial ventures include a hugely popular YouTube channel, did not reveal his future competitive plans, beyond a scheduled appearance at next month's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa.

But the famously outspoken and self-confident star vowed to act with "humility and respect" in the future as he ponders his next step.

"Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," he said.

"Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me."

Beyond the Nedbank Golf Challenge event, "I'll go about whatever is next the right way," he added.

articles.title: Blades Brown at 19 becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years. Rahm win in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: LOS CABOS, Mexico (AP) — Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years Sunday when the 19-year-old rallied from a seven-shot deficit with a 9-...
articles.body:
LOS CABOS, Mexico (AP) — Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years Sunday when the 19-year-old rallied from a seven-shot deficit with a 9-under 63 and beat Ben James with a birdie on the second playoff hole in the World Wide Technology Championship.

Brown became the youngest winner since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA.

James lost a four-shot lead going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante and then showed his moxie by smoking a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-5 18th and making eagle to salvage a 70 and force the playoff.

But he missed an 8-foot putt on the second playoff hole, and Brown made his 3-footer.

ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — Jon Rahm fought off Ryder Cup teammates Rory McIlroy and Tyrrell Hatton to win the Abu Dhabi Championship on Sunday for his first European tour title in four years and his first start since the demise of LIV Golf.

Rahm shot 5-under 67 at Yas Links and finished two shots ahead of Hatton (68) and four ahead of McIlroy (69) in the first of the two season-ending playoff tournaments in the United Arab Emirates.

This was Rahm's first event in seven weeks, during which time his wife gave birth to their fourth child and he finalized his departure from LIV Golf. The victory moves him back into the top 10 in the world ranking.

McIlroy moved to No. 2 in the Race to Dubai, 534 points behind Eugenio Chacarra. The title will be decided next week at the DP World Tour Championship, which McIlroy has won three times.

OMITAMA, Japan (AP) — Shuri Sakuma became the fifth Japanese player to win on the LPGA Tour this season, closing with an 8-under 64 for a four-shot victory in the Toto Classic.

Sakuma won for the fifth time on the Japan LPGA this year, after a four-win season in 2025. The victory makes her eligible to join the LPGA Tour. She finished at 20-under 268.

Aki Iwai, who had a one-shot lead going into the final round, closed with a 71 to finish second. Erika Hara finished a career-best third after a 70 at the Taiheiyo Club north of Tokyo, moving Hara to No. 32 in the Race to CME Globe.

Yuta Ikeda closed with a 4-under 67l and won a three-man playoff to capture the ACN Championship on the Japan Tour. Ikeda won after Kohei Okada made bogey on the first playoff hole, and Ryunosoke Furukawa Kohei failed to match Ikeda's par on the fourth playoff hole. ... Ana Pelaez Trivino rallied from five shots behind with a 9-under 64, winning the Aramco China Championship by three shots over Mimi Rhodes on the Ladies European Tour. ... Louis Albertse closed with a 4-under 68 for a three-shot victory in the Telkom PGA Championship on the Sunshine Tour in South Africa. ... Jean Hugo closed with a 7-under 65 to win the European Senior Masters in Spain for his third win in as many starts on the Legends Tour. ... Hyunjo Yoo shot 4-under 68 and won the Daebo HausD Championship by one shot on the Korea LPGA.

articles.title: 49ers ride takeaways, effective ground game to win over Raiders and 7-1 record
articles.summary: The 49ers got three interceptions and two fumble recoveries from the defense and the offense had 190 yards rushing in their win over the Raiders at Levi's St...
articles.body:
On a day in which the San Francisco 49ers ' new-look defensive line largely struggled to generate pressure, it was the back end of the defense that created action.

The 49ers, who beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on Sunday at Levi's Stadium, entered the day with seven takeaways in seven games. On Sunday, they had five - all in the second half - during a stretch of complete domination for that unit. A Las Vegas offense led by quarterback Kirk Cousins, despite having plenty of opportunities to cut its deficit to one possession while the 49ers' offense struggled out of the half, repeatedly gave the ball away.

The results of the Raiders' opening five drives after halftime: pick-six, touchdown, fumble, fumble, interception.

San Francisco owes much of that to its trio of starting linebackers. Rookie Jaden Dugger took the first play of the second half to the house. Two drives later, Fred Warner punched the ball out at the 26-yard line (his fifth forced fumble of the season) and Dre Greenlaw recovered at the 31. On the ensuing possession, defensive back Upton Stout did his best Warner impression, punching the ball free from Raiders tight end Michael Mayer's grasp as he extended into the end zone; Warner recovered, keeping Las Vegas from cutting its deficit to four.

On the next drive, San Francisco's defense looked to be in trouble again. A 33-yard completion to tight end Brock Bowers brought the Raiders to the 1-yard line. Cousins attempted a quarterback sneak, and Warner dove over the pile to knock him back two yards. Two plays later, cornerback Renardo Green leaped to intercept a ball intended for Tre Tucker in the right corner of the end zone. Safety Malik Mustapha added an interception for good measure in garbage time.

Not a bad stretch for defensive coordinator Raheem Morris' unit.

SF: McCaffrey 1 run (Pineiro kick), 9:32.

SF: McCaffrey 12 pass from Purdy (Pineiro kick), 5:14.

SF: Dugger 35 interception return (Pineiro kick), 14:43.

Las: Bowers 21 pass from Cousins (Gay kick), 9:29.

SF: Watkins 37 pass from Purdy (Pineiro kick), :36.

RUSHING: Las Vegas, Jeanty 6-25, Bowers 1-2, Cousins 2-0, Washington 6-(minus 3). San Francisco, Black 11-70, McCaffrey 18-68, Purdy 7-40, James 3-11, Juszczyk 1-4, Jones 3-(minus 3).

PASSING: Las Vegas, Cousins 22-32-3-216. San Francisco, Purdy 17-25-1-232.

RECEIVING: Las Vegas, Bowers 7-111, Jeanty 5-(minus 5), Tucker 4-55, Mayer 3-37, Nailor 2-9, Bech 1-9. San Francisco, Watkins 4-86, Kittle 4-58, Robinson 3-22, Cooks 2-25, McCaffrey 2-19, Hodge 1-17, Cowing 1-5.

Run, run the ball: The Raiders entered Sunday allowing a league-worst 5.1 yards per rushing attempt. They gave up 365 yards on the ground in their previous two games entering Sunday. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan was well aware of this fact, telling the Fox broadcast pregame he was aiming to have a 40-carry game.

San Francisco ended the afternoon with a season-high of 43 runs, with the caveat that a number of those came on the game's final drive with the result sealed.

The 49ers managed 25 rushes in the first half alone, gaining 125 yards on the ground for two touchdowns. Quarterback Brock Purdy threw the ball only 12 times before the break, averaging 10.3 yards per attempt for 123 yards.

In the second half, the 49ers strayed a bit from that strategy. Twelve rushes to 13 passes to start the period was a far cry from the first-half ratio, but San Francisco still managed to gain 4.4 yards per rush and 190 yards on the ground.

Purdy alone racked up a season-high 40 rushing yards on seven attempts and scored a touchdown. Christian McCaffrey ran 18 times for 68 yards and a score, and rookie backup Kaelon Black toted the ball 11 times for 70 yards.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel Delivers Blunt Assessment of Drake Maye After Patriots Loss
articles.summary: The Patriots quarterback threw three interceptions in a four-turnover loss to Green Bay.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots had a night to forget against the Green Bay Packers, and head coach Mike Vrabel didn't try to sugarcoat it.

New England committed four turnovers in its Week 9 loss, with Drake Maye throwing three interceptions. Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards and three touchdowns, but his turnovers put the Patriots in an early hole and made it difficult to keep pace with Green Bay.

"We lost, and we got our asses kicked," Vrabel told reporters after the game. "There's no two ways around it. Like, that's what happened tonight."

The Patriots coach pointed to several areas that need improvement, including tackling, pressuring the quarterback and creating turnovers defensively. He also stressed the importance of maintaining offensive balance rather than becoming too reliant on the passing game when trailing.

Maye's performance was a significant part of the problem. Vrabel admitted he was disappointed by how the quarterback's afternoon unfolded.

"I'm surprised about, you know, just the way that the day went, the way that it started, and then I guess kind of how the third quarter went," Vrabel said.

Maye took responsibility for his mistakes, acknowledging that his turnovers put the defense in difficult positions and prevented the offense from building momentum.

"Starting with me, man, it's one of the biggest differences between winning and losing football games," Maye said. "And so, you know, our defense in a bad spot, you know, in the first drive. And just, you know, gave them the football."

The quarterback also admitted he was late on some throws and needed to do a better job with his decision-making and communication.

"I'm sure disappointed in myself. You can't put the team in the hole, you know, straight off the bat," Maye said. "And we had chances to, you know, put us back within three points, you know, multiple times. And just frustrating."

Despite the disappointing result, Vrabel emphasized that the Patriots need to move forward together and show how they'll respond.

"Losing is frustrating," Vrabel said. "We're in this together. We're going to get them back and get ready to travel and put 48 guys out there that care and want to exhibit some sort of identity, and see how we respond."

articles.title: Jon Rahm Wins $1.5 Million but Still Down $100 Million from LIV
articles.summary: Jon Rahm won his first tournament after leaving LIV Golf, earning $1.53 million while still owed over $100 million by the collapsed league.
articles.body:
Jon Rahm secured his first tournament victory since departing LIV Golf on Sunday, claiming the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship with a final score of 23-under par. The Spanish golfer finished two strokes ahead of Tyrrell Hatton and four shots clear of Rory McIlroy at Yas Links. This win marks a return to form for Rahm, who had not won on the DP World Tour since November 2022. Despite the triumph, the financial reality of his exit remains stark: he forfeited over $100 million in potential earnings by leaving the breakaway circuit.

The Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship offered a total purse of $9 million, with Rahm taking home the winner's check of $1.53 million. According to Celebrity Net Worth, this prize money represents only about 1.43 percent of the funds LIV Golf still owed him at the time of his departure. The league, which declared bankruptcy and officially folded this year, had promised massive payouts to its top players. Rahm was the league's individual champion in each of its seasons, yet he chose to walk away from the guaranteed money when the terms of a potential LIV 2.0 became unacceptable.

Rahm's victory on Sunday followed a seven-week break that saw the birth of his second daughter and his final departure from the now-defunct LIV Golf league. The Spaniard admitted that mental battles and external distractions had hampered his recent play leading up to this event. "After everything that's gone on," Rahm said, according to Yahoo Sports , "and some poor play and some battles mentally with a lot of noise, to come back out after a bit of rest and being with the family, it's quite special." His last regular-tour win on the European circuit came at the World Tour Championship in November 2022, just before his controversial move to the Saudi-backed league.

Three birdies across five holes beginning at the 11th hole allowed Rahm to surge ahead, demanding precision and patience in the final round for victory. He shot a 5-under 67 to finish the week, while Hatton carded a 68 and McIlroy posted a 69. Rahm described his performance on the final day as nearly perfect despite a single error. "As far as I'm concerned, except the (tee) shot on No. 17, I played a pretty flawless round," said Rahm, who banked a winner's check of $1.5 million. "It was really, really something." This result propelled him from 51st to sixth in the overall Race to Dubai standings.

The top two finishers at the Abu Dhabi event were both former LIV Golf members, signaling a potential trend of players returning to established tours after the breakaway circuit's collapse. Tyrrell Hatton, who finished second and earned $990,000, had played with Rahm on the Legion XIII team during the LIV era. Rory McIlroy, who finished third and took home $563,000, has been one of the most vocal critics of LIV Golf throughout its existence. The presence of these high-profile players suggests the DP World Tour is regaining its competitive depth as the alternative league winds down operations.

Winning the Race to Dubai title remains possible for Rahm next week if he secures victory at the DP World Tour Championship. This singular win has already demonstrated his ability to compete at the highest level without the financial guarantees of his previous contract. While he may never fully recoup the $100 million he left on the table, the win proves his game remains sharp. DP World Tour leadership and the circuit itself are expected to receive a major boost from his return to European golf in 2027.

The financial toll of Rahm's decision remains a defining aspect of his career transition. Reports indicate the league owed him $7 million in unpaid wages, and his departure cost him an additional $100 million in future guarantees. According to Celebrity Net Worth, Rahm accepted the decision to leave all that money behind and separate from LIV Golf. The league's funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund ended earlier this year, leading to a rapid unraveling of the organization's financial structure. With the league now bankrupt, Rahm's decision to leave before the final collapse may have saved his long-term reputation despite the immediate cash loss.

Rahm's performance on Sunday confirms he is ready to rebuild his legacy on the traditional tours. "From last to first is a pretty good feeling," he told reporters here in Abu Dhabi, referencing his rapid ascent in the standings, according to Today's Golfer . With a new life stage approaching, the Spaniard has once again become one of the world's top golfers. This victory is a strong start to his post-LIV career, even if the financial debt from the breakaway league remains unpaid. The DP World Tour now has a major star competing in its season-ending events.

articles.title: Blades Brown Makes PGA Tour History as Youngest Winner in 95 Years After 7-Shot Comeback
articles.summary: Blades Brown made history on Sunday.
articles.body:
Not only did the 19-year-old overcome a seven-stroke deficit to win the World Wide Technology Championship following a pair of playoff holes, he also became the youngest player to win on the PGA Tour in nearly 100 years.

According to the Associated Press , "Brown became the youngest winner since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA."

Brown shot a 9-under 63 on Sunday and registered birdies on both playoff holes to secure the historic victory, besting Ben James.

"I'm so obsessed with this game. It tests you in so many ways," Brown told reporters. "I love golf, all the stuff that goes into it and I can't wait for what's next."

articles.title: Mumbai AQI 30% better than last Diwali's, but plunges at night
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Diwali celebrations began with the city enjoying much cleaner air over last year's but the quality plunged to poor/hazardous at several places
articles.body: MUMBAI: Diwali celebrations began with the city enjoying much cleaner air over last year's but the quality plunged to poor/hazardous at several places amid the firecracker-bursting. In the murk glistened a thin silver lining: firecracker noise levels are down compared to two decades ago, coinciding with increasing use of green crackers and more public awareness.The city's AQI was 132 on Sunday, almost a 30% improvement from the 188 recorded during the same period last year. But the PM 2.5 level that stood at a 42 in Andheri at 8pm, soared to 597 just 2 hours later; it was 606 at Malad. Chembur had a PM10 level of 480 at 10pm.Environmental activists caution noise pollution too remains well above permissible limits in many residential areas and stricter enforcement is needed. "So far, the overall noise levels are lower than previous years. But one needs to check if firecrackers are burst late Sunday night," said anti-noise pollution activist Sumaira Abdulali of Awaaz Foundation.A recent study by Awaaz Foundation and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) found peak firecracker noise levels have fallen sharply over the last 20 years (see box). RTI activist Anil Galgali agreed noise levels were lower, crediting awareness campaigns and court orders.‘Awareness drives, court orders pushed noise levels down’Peak readings during a pre-Diwali testing of firecrackers this year touched 93 decibels (dB), substantially lower than the 144.9 dB recorded in 2006, a recent Awaaz Foundation and MPCB study showed.While the Mumbai and Thane District Fireworks Dealers Welfare Association described this year’s cracker sales as “largely normal”, several retailers across the city reported a decline in demand compared to previous years.According to association’s honorary general secretary Minesh N Mehta, firecracker sales had dropped to around 70% by the end of Ganeshotsav, but business picked up through Navratri and Diwali after an initially slow start. “Most crackers available today are green crackers and consumers have accepted them over the last five years. Sales have been broadly normal, though trends vary from area to area,” Mehta said.However, traders on the ground painted a more nuanced picture. A Vile Parle dealer said sales were lower than last year as many customers deliberately reduced purchases owing to environmental concerns. A Malad shop owner noted that children themselves were urging parents to buy fewer crackers and opt for green varieties such as sparklers and ground spinners. Bombay High Court had also recently ruled that celebrities should voluntarily help spread awareness against firecracker pollution without charging any public moneyTOI spoke to residents, activists and political leaders attributing the change to greater environmental awareness and compliance with court directions. RTI activist Anil Galgali said noise levels were lower, crediting awareness drives and court orders, though political events in some areas may have caused localised spikes.Andheri resident Karan Jotwani said both cracker sales and bursting had visibly declined in the Lokhandwala area. “The number of cracker stalls has reduced and even in my 240-flat housing society, noise was nearly half of previous years. I also think people are becoming more conscious. I was especially worried as I have a pet at home now,” he said.Shiv Sena corporator Amey Ghole said greater public awareness had encouraged many people to either avoid crackers or opt for green fireworks. “So, there was more focus on the traditional and environmentally friendly options this Diwali. The celebrations were more cultural and less loud which is a welcome move. We are all for celebrations that are environmentally friendly,” Ghole said. BJP MLA Mihir Kotecha said most citizens followed the HC directive by bursting crackers within housing complexes and grounds rather than on public roads.Former Congress corporator Sheetal Mhatre also observed a decline in cracker noise, adding that rising living costs and higher cracker prices may have prompted many households to cut back on purchases this year.But Abdulali pointed out that even 93 dB exceeds prescribed ambient noise limits for residential, commercial, industrial and silence zones. In a representation to the state govt, she urged authorities to strengthen enforcement of noise regulations, particularly during Diwali. In her letter to CM Devendra Fadnavis, she also highlighted that Mumbai has 110 notified silence zones where bursting firecrackers is prohibited. articles.title: Jon Rahm: How DP World Tour win in Abu Dhabi marks start of 'next page' in career after mental strain of LIV Golf exit
articles.summary: Jon Rahm opened up about the arrival of his fourth child and the challenges of his LIV Golf League exit after his Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship win - his sixth Rolex Series victory and first DP World Tour title since The Masters in April 2023
articles.body:
Rahm returned from a seven-week absence to make his debut at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, where a two-shot win marked his 11th DP World Tour title and his first since April 2023.

The Rolex Series event was his first start since finishing rock-bottom at September's BMW PGA Championship, where Rahm's mind was focused primarily on the possibility of his impending fourth child arriving early.

Rahm's wife Kelley welcomed their daughter Begona in mid-October and the Spaniard's playing future has also since been made clearer, having made a separation agreement with LIV Golf ahead of them 'winding down operations'.

The former world No 1 failed to win on the DP World Tour during his three seasons with LIV Golf, but victory over Ryder Cup teammates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy is a record sixth Rolex Series victory.

"It [winning] means a lot," Rahm said. "It's been quite a while since I've played good in a DP World Tour event. From last [BMW PGA Championship] to first is a pretty good feeling."

He added: "To battle it out with Tyrrell [Hatton], who is the other man with five [Rolex Series wins], to break the tie and get it done - he's a good friend of mine and I know how good a competitor he is. It's a special week."

Rahm's attorney told a bankruptcy court last month that he would not be participating with any proposed 'LIV 2.0', having topped the individual standings in all three seasons on the circuit and won four of their events.

He has faced regular questions about his - and the league's future - throughout the season, although can now turn his attention to featuring more frequently on the DP World Tour.

"Whether you like to admit it or not, it [LIV Golf] was a lot of extra noise going on in general, and that was still not the most important part of my life," he said.

"In the sense of the impending birth of our daughter was something that was weighing heavily on me at Wentworth, I'm not going to lie, I didn't want to miss it. It was a little bit more difficult to perhaps play and think throughout the golf course [when] it felt a little bit cloudy in a sense.

"The calmness I felt this week has been enjoyable all week, honestly. I felt incredible calm, even when things didn't go anyway. Not much seemed to bother me, and probably the main reason why I was able to perform the way I have."

On whether the demise of LIV Golf marked the end of one chapter of his career, Rahm said: "One could say that.

"After everything that's gone on, and some poor play and some battles mentally with a lot of noise, to come back out after a bit of rest and having a new addition to the family, it's quite special."

Rahm said pre-tournament that he not talked with the PGA Tour about a potential return, while his win in Abu Dhabi keeps his hopes alive of winning the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai this season.

"I don't know how else to say it - it's on to the next page, right," Rahm explained. "Luckily in golf, I've been fortunate to have a lot of opportunities and take advantage of them.

Rahm is one of nine players now with a mathematical chance of winning the Race to Dubai, although needs to win the DP World Tour Championship for a fourth time and require both Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy's results to go in his favour.

"I didn't think I would ever have a chance to win it [Race to Dubai]," Rahm added. "I'm very excited - it actually gives me a little extra incentive next week.

"Those are better odds than I expected so looking forward to it and hopefully I can get my fourth one [DP World Tour Championship]."

The DP World Tour season reaches its climax next week at the DP World Tour Championship, where only the top 50 available players in the Race to Dubai standings are eligible to compete.

articles.title: Green shoots spring up in Exeter park hit by wildfire
articles.summary: A country park was devastated by fire but the speed of nature's recovery surprises wildlife experts.
articles.body:
Nature is beginning to return to a country park two months after a devastating wildfire, bosses have said.

Devon Wildlife Trust, which manages the site on behalf of Exeter City Council, said green bramble bushes, wildflowers and various small birds and mammals were re-establishing in the charred landscape.

Randy Mayers, from the trust, said the park had seen a "second spurt of growth, almost like a second spring".

The trust said grassland, shrub and hedgerow homes of animals including songbirds, butterflies, moths, harvest mice and field voles had all been affected by the fire.

At the time of the blaze experts said nature could be resilient and it was hoped then the area could thrive once again.

However, Mayers said the trust was surprised regrowth could be seen so quickly.

Wildflowers growing in scorched areas was a "sign of recovery and a healthy meadow", he added.

"We've seen lots of flowers out, lots of birds, and we've seen rabbits and few harvest mice so they haven't all been decimated, which is great news," he said.

Duncan Wood, from Exeter City Council, said the authority would allow the trust to lead the park's recovery as "they are the experts".

He said the council was "firmly behind behind them, and will provide whatever support they need".

articles.title: How Israel’s separation wall compares with the Berlin Wall
articles.summary: How Israel’s wall, checkpoints and permits divide Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and cut farmers off from land.
articles.body:
In the occupied West Bank, a barrier of concrete and fencing cuts Palestinians off from their land, their families and nearby towns.

Israel began building its separation wall in 2002. Planned to stretch 712km (442 miles), it runs deep inside Palestinian territory rather than along the boundary with Israel. In 2004, the International Court of Justice ruled it illegal.

Today’s date carries extra weight. Thirty-seven years ago on November 9, 1989, the Berlin Wall fell.

Built by East Germany in 1961 to stop its citizens fleeing to the West, it encircled West Berlin for 155km (96 miles), dividing the city and its people for 28 years.

Since 2003, Palestinians have marked the same date as an international day of action against Israel’s wall, which is more than four times as long and still being built. In urban areas, its concrete rises to about 9 metres (30ft), more than twice the height of Berlin’s.

But the wall is more than a physical structure. It operates alongside a wider network of checkpoints, roadblocks, gates and permits that restricts Palestinian movement across the occupied territory.

According to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), about 456km (283 miles), or 64 percent, of the planned route had been built by April.

About 85 percent of it runs inside the West Bank rather than along the Green Line, the 1949 armistice line separating Israel from the West Bank. That route determines which communities, roads and farmland are cut off from their surroundings.

In some urban areas, the barrier is a concrete wall. Elsewhere, it is made up of fences, patrol roads, ditches and other security infrastructure.

For Palestinians, the comparison with Berlin carries a message. “It doesn’t matter how high the barriers will be, they will fall,” a Palestinian activist in Bir Nabala told Al Jazeera. “Like the Berlin Wall fell, the Palestinian wall will fall.”

How many people are cut off from their land?

The wall’s impact reaches far beyond the structure itself. Its route cuts Palestinian communities off from neighbouring towns, workplaces and farmland, disrupting livelihoods and everyday life.

More than 14,000 Palestinians live between the wall and the Green Line in an area known as the Seam Zone. To reach basic services, markets and relatives on the other side, they must pass through checkpoints.

Farmers are among the hardest hit. According to OCHA, about 150 Palestinian communities have land in this area. Reaching it depends on permits, prior coordination with Israeli authorities and access through designated agricultural gates.

There are about 62 such gates along the wall, and most stay closed for much of the year. During the 2025 olive harvest, 74 percent opened only on a limited number of days.

In Qalqiliya, the wall wraps around much of the city, cutting it off from nearby Palestinian communities and the land around it. Journeys to neighbouring towns that were once short can now mean passing through checkpoints or taking long detours.

The wall restricts more than movement. It reshapes how communities relate to their land and places that are part of their everyday lives.

The wall is only one part of a much wider network restricting Palestinian movement across the West Bank.

As of December, OCHA documented 925 checkpoints, road gates, earth mounds and other obstacles across the West Bank and occupied East Jerusalem. They restrict the movement of about 3.4 million Palestinians, often forcing long detours to reach work, school, hospitals and other services.

The network includes 89 permanently staffed checkpoints, 218 partial checkpoints, 232 road gates, 167 earth mounds, 114 linear closures and 105 roadblocks.

Checkpoints and road gates now make up nearly 60 percent of these obstacles, up from 15 percent two decades ago when temporary blockages, such as earth mounds and roadblocks, were far more common.

Crossing the wall itself requires permits. Of its 13 checkpoints, only three can be used by Palestinians with West Bank IDs and Israeli-issued permits to enter East Jerusalem and Israel. OCHA said these permits are hard to get and many have been revoked or suspended since the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023.

The wall stretches for hundreds of kilometres, but its impact cannot be measured by distance alone. It is measured in the farmland farmers struggle to reach, the communities cut off from nearby towns and the checkpoints between people and the places they need to go.

articles.title: World Wide Technology Championship: Teenager Blades Brown becomes youngest PGA Tour tournament winner in 95 years
articles.summary: Blades Brown also becomes first teenager to win on the PGA Tour since Jordan Spieth in 2013 at 19 years and 171 days old; he came back from a deficit of seven shots with a nine-under 63 to defeat Ben James in the World Wide Technology Championship
articles.body:
At 19 years and 171 days old, Brown became the youngest victor since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA.

James lost a four-shot lead going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante and then showed his nerve by smoking a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-five 18th and making eagle to salvage a 70 and force the play-off.

But he missed an eight-foot putt on the second play-off hole as Brown made his three-footer.

"It hasn't set in just yet, I guess, the magnitude of being a PGA Tour winner," Brown said. "Golf is one of the best games, is one of the greatest games in the world. It challenges you mentally, physically, spiritually. It challenges you in every aspect of us, right?

"I just go back to five-year-old Blades that was watching the TV and watching Tiger Woods and all those great players win major championships, and to think that I'm now in a similar spot with having won a PGA Tour event is mind-blowing."

Brown turned pro at 17 and earned his PGA Tour card this year by being among the top 20 in Korn Ferry Tour points.

"I'm so obsessed with this game. It tests you in so many ways," Brown said. "I love golf, all the stuff that goes into it, and I can't wait for what's next."

With eight players separated by two shots on the back nine, Brown ran off three straight birdies to share the lead and then left the mistakes to everyone else.

He hit a superb pitch for birdie on the final hole to post a score of 23-under 265.

That put him one shot ahead of Michael Kim, who played with the Tennessee teen and made birdie from 12 feet for 64 right before Brown made his putt.

Brown now has a two-year exemption, which puts him in the elite Championship Series when the PGA Tour's new model begins in 2028.

The victory also assures Brown of his first major next year at the PGA Championship.

It was another setback for James, who in 13 starts since turning pro has five finishes in the top five, and two runner-up finishes.

articles.standfirst: Con 19 años gana el WW Technology Championship en el segundo hoyo de desempate remontando siete golpes. Su madre anotó el primer triple de la historia de la WNBA
articles.summary: Con 19 años gana el WW Technology Championship en el segundo hoyo de desempate remontando siete golpes. Su madre anotó el primer triple de la historia de la WNBA
articles.body: Blades Brown es hoy el hombre que acapara titulares en los informativos deportivos de Estados Unidos. Alimentado el sector de una permanente búsqueda de un nuevo talento, una nueva cara con la que llamar la atención de la audencia, Brown se ha convertido en el ganador más joven del PGA Tour de la era moderna, al imponerse con 19 años, 5 meses y 18 días en el WW Technology Chamipionship. Su marca rejuvenece en seis meses el registro que Jordan Spieth fijó en el John Deere Classic de 2013 y se sitúa la cuarta de todos los tiempos de una lista que encabeza Charles Kocsis, el único que ganó un título con 18 años (6 meses y 9 días), cuando venció en el Michigan Open en 1931. Su triunfo habla bien de él por cómo se produjo. Porque consiguió con una tarjeta de 63 golpes remontar siete golpes de diferencia en la última jornada para alcanzar un desempate; porque soportó la tensión de dos hoyos de playoff para levantar el título. Un birdie desde 1,5 metros definió el pulso frente a Ben James. (Resultados) Más nombres ilustres quedarán asociadas a este chico nacido en Nashville y cuya madre Rondha Blades es parte de la historia del deporte al ser la primera mujer de la WNBA que anotó un triple en 1998. Tiger Woods es el diseñador del recorrido del Cardonal, en Los Cabos, donde se produjo su hazaña. Se une así al de Bobby Jones (18 años en 1920), al que había sacado de los libros del US Amateur en 2023, al ser el más precoz, con 16 años, en liderar -con otros dos golfistas- la fase de stroke play de la gran cita del golf aficionado. Para rematar el gran relato familiar, hace cuatro años su padre fue diagnosticado con un cáncer de huesos. Los médicos le dieron un año de vida. Posteriormente, otro diagnóstico descubrió que era una leucemia de células vellosas, no curable, pero sí tratable. El domingo pudo ver y grabar en el móvil la primera victoria profesional de su único hijo. Sus hazañas entre las logradas por los afamados culminan con que en 2024 fue nombrado mejor junior del mundo con el Rolex Junior Player of the Year de la AJGA, un premio que antes habían ganado Woods, Spieth y Scheffler. Brown se saltó la universidad para saltar al profesionalismo cuando tenía 17 años y tras pasar por el Korn Ferry Tour, la liga de desarrollo, que alternó con algunas invitaciones al PGA Tour, ahora se ha coronado. "Es un talento increíble", dijo Michael Kim, quien jugó junto a Brown en la ronda final y quedó a un golpe del desempate. "Creo que podría ser el mejor de todos los jóvenes con los que he jugado. La forma en que golpea la bola es algo que solo los verdaderos talentos del golf pueden lograr". El nuevo talento ya había emitido señales en el circuito esta temporada cuando tiró 60 golpes en el American Express y cuando acabó tercero en el Abierto de Puerto Rico. Hace un mes había conseguido la tarjeta de la gran liga a través del Korn Ferry. "Recuerdo cuando tenía 5 años y veía en la televisión a Tiger Woods y a todos esos grandes jugadores ganar campeonatos importantes", dijo Brown. "Pensar que ahora estoy en una posición similar, habiendo ganado un torneo del PGA Tour, es alucinante".

articles.title: WTGL: Los Angeles Golf Club make history by winning inaugural match against New York at SoFi Center
articles.summary: The inaugural WTGL season teed off at SoFi Center in Florida with Los Angeles Golf Club defeating New York Golf Club; the opener included walk-up videos from the parking lot, flashy intros for the fans on hand, some funky fashion and Serena Williams in attendance
articles.body:
Lydia Ko and Michelle Wie West were among the six players in action who treated an audience of 1,500 fans at the indoor venue in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida to some spectacular shot-making, several dramatic near-misses and pure entertainment between the mic'd-up players.

Wie West, Alison Lee and Gaby Lopez eventually out-duelled Rose Zhang and her team-mates in Linn Grant and Ko.

New York's Zhang broke new ground as she hit the first tee shot, one that she blasted 301 yards into the fairway on Cut The Sails.

Wie West came agonisingly close to registering a hole-in-in-one at the par-three seventh as Los Angeles built a narrow 2-1 lead over New York after the first nine holes of team play. New York took number 5, and Lee took down Grant on number 11

In the closing holes, New York had chances, but Zhang missed two short putts on the 13th hole and Grant missed a 10-foot putt on the 14th.

That secured the win for Los Angeles, 3-1, before the teams tied the final hole.

"Our purses are growing up, and we get to play the most amazing golf courses we've ever played," Lee said. "For people to experience and see us play in a different setting, in a more intimate and personal setting, is very different, and hopefully it can bring more eyeballs to the game."

Los Angeles will have a chance to build a verifiable winning streak on Tuesday as the inaugural season begins to ramp up.

Wie West and co will take on Motor City Golf Club, who boast a line-up led by Lexi Thompson and Brooke Henderson.

The WTGL follows on from the success of the Tomorrow's Golf League (TGL), founded by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy's TMRW Sports, in partnership with the PGA Tour.

The women's edition of the tech-infused golf league will see LPGA Tour stars feature in a unique team format, with five teams (representing five different cities) of five-player rosters confirmed for the inaugural season.

The season-long competition takes place across November and December at the SoFi Center in Florida, a purpose-built indoor venue, with every shot live and all the players mic'd up for the made-for-TV format.

Both the 2026 and 2027 editions of WTGL will be broadcast exclusively on Sky Sports as part of an expansion of its golf rights, which also includes a further two years of TGL presented by SoFi.

articles.title: Blades Brown, 19, becomes youngest PGA Tour winner since 1938
articles.summary: Teenager Blades Brown beats Ben James at the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico to become the youngest PGA Tour tournament winner since 1938.

Nineteen-year-old Blades Brown became the youngest winner on the PGA Tour in 95 years with a thrilling victory in the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico.

Brown beat fellow American Ben James on the second play-off hole in Cabo San Lucas after shooting a nine-under-par 63, which included a birdie on the 18th, to come from seven shots behind.

At 19 years and 171 days, he is the youngest PGA winner since 18-year-old Charles Kocsis won the 1931 Michigan Open, which was considered a regional event in the early years of the tour.

Brown is the first teenage PGA winner since Jordan Spieth won the John Deere Classic in 2013 at 19 years and 352 days.

"It hasn't set in just yet, the magnitude of being a PGA Tour winner," Brown said.

"I just go back to five-year-old Blades that was watching the TV and watching Tiger Woods and all those great players win major championships, and to think that I'm now in a similar spot with them having won a PGA Tour event is mind-blowing.

"I'm so obsessed with this game. It tests you in so many ways. I love golf, all the stuff that goes into it, and I can't wait for what's next."

Brown and James finished on 23 under, with American Michael Kim in third on 22 under and Kensei Hirata a shot further back.

Brown, who turned professional at 17, finished in the top 20 on the Korn Ferry Tour points list earlier this year, which secured his PGA Tour card.

articles.summary: The Open Championship will return to Carnoustie in 2029, for the first time in 11 years.
articles.body:
The Open Championship will return to Carnoustie in 2029, for the first time in 11 years.

Francesco Molinari won the 2018 event at the Angus course, which also hosted the last time a Scottish winner took the Claret Jug when Paul Lawrie triumphed in 1999.

Other Carnoustie Open winners include Padraig Harrington (2007), Tom Watson (1975) and Gary Player (1968).

In all, the course has hosted the event eight times since 1931.

New Zealand's Ryan Fox won this year's Open at Royal Birkdale, the 2027 event will be at the Old Course in St Andrews and the 2028 staging will be at Royal Lytham.

The 157th Open will be played from 19-22 July, 2029.

And Royal & Ancient Club chief executive Mark Darbon commented: "Carnoustie is a world-class championship venue where some of golf's greatest players have lifted the Claret Jug and the return of The Open to these famous links after more than a decade will give fans the opportunity to be part of another memorable chapter in the championship's history.

"We want to continue to deliver an outstanding experience for players, fans and our partners at one of the world's great sporting events and so have worked closely in collaboration with Carnoustie to help ensure their plans to enhance the venue also support successful stagings of The Open in the years ahead."

articles.title: The Open: Carnoustie announced by R&A as host venue for The 157th Open in 2029
articles.summary: Carnoustie's Championship Course will host The 157th Open in 2029, the first time the Scottish links has held the event since Francesco Molinari's 2018 win; Paul Lawrie and Padraig Harrington are other past winners at that venue
articles.body:
The 157th Open will be played on the Championship Course from July 19-22 that year, the ninth time the Scottish course has hosted the event.

Golf's original championship was last held at Carnoustie in 2018, when Francesco Molinari lifted the Claret Jug and was crowned Champion Golfer of the Year.

Tommy Armour, Sir Henry Cotton, Ben Hogan, Gary Player, Tom Watson, Paul Lawrie and Padraig Harrington are the other golfers to have previously won The Open at that venue.

Mark Darbon, chief executive of The R&A, said: " Carnoustie is a world-class championship venue where some of golf's greatest players have lifted the Claret Jug.

"The return of The Open to these famous links, after more than a decade, will give fans the opportunity to be part of another memorable chapter in the Championship's history.

"We want to continue to deliver an outstanding experience for players, fans and our partners at one of the world's great sporting events and so have worked closely in collaboration with Carnoustie to help ensure their plans to enhance the venue also support successful stagings of The Open in the years ahead.

"We are grateful to Carnoustie's ownership and management, the Scottish Government and local authorities for their support in bringing The Open back to Angus and look forward to another memorable Championship in 2029."

Carnoustie has also hosted three editions of The Senior Open, most recently for KJ Choi's 2024 success, while Anna Nordqvist won the AIG Women's Open there in 2021.

Scotland's First Minister John Swinney said: "The return of The Open to Carnoustie Golf Links in 2029 is tremendous news for Scotland. As the home of golf, we have a unique connection to this historic championship and are proud to welcome it back to one of the sport's most renowned venues.

"The Open generates significant benefits for our economy, supports jobs and tourism and shines a global spotlight on Scotland's people, places and outstanding golf offering."

The Open will take place on the iconic Old Course at St Andrews in 2027 and return to Royal Lytham & St Annes - for a one-off August date - the following year, with no venues yet confirmed beyond Carnoustie hosting the 2029 edition.

articles.summary: Gurgaon’s post-Diwali AQI rose to 345 but stayed “very poor,” not “severe,” making it the third-cleanest post-festival day in 10 years due to wind.
articles.body: Gurgaon: Firecracker emissions pushed pollution levels up in Gurgaon after Diwali, with the city’s air quality index (AQI) rising 57 points from 288 on Diwali (Nov 8) to 345 on Monday. But thanks to wind, the air quality marginally improved on Sunday, and Monday’s overall pollution level wasn’t any worse than the pre-Diwali level (345), remaining ‘very poor’ but not going into ‘severe’ as feared.As a result, this year’s post-Diwali air is the third-cleanest in the last 10 years. Only 2022 and 2024 recorded cleaner air after the festival, at 292 and 309, respectively.Between 2016 and 2026, the average post-Diwali AQI stood at 381.5, nearly 30% higher than the pre-Diwali average of 293.1. The average reading on Diwali day was 319.2. This year marked the first time in a decade that the city’s AQI remained unchanged between the pre-Diwali and post-Diwali days. The only other instances of an improvement after Diwali were in 2022, when the post-Diwali AQI improved to 292 (poor) from 322 on the festival day, and in 2019, when it was marginally better at 368 from 372 on Diwali.The worst post-Diwali air quality was recorded in 2021, when the AQI surged to 472 (severe), up from 330 on the pre-Diwali day and 395 on Diwali. In 2020, when the city recorded its worst Diwali AQI in a decade at 425, pollution levels climbed further to 460 the following day, against 324 before the festival.Last year, the post-Diwali AQI stood at 370, significantly higher than 294 on Diwali and 245 on the preceding day. In 2023, the post-Diwali AQI deteriorated sharply to 349, from 199 on the pre-Diwali day and 193 on Diwali, despite two days of unexpected, widespread rainfall ahead of the festival.A complete ban on firecrackers was in force from 2020 to 2025. This year, however, restrictions were eased after Supreme Court granted conditional approval for the use of certified green crackers across Delhi-NCR on Nov 7 and 8. Only CSIR-NEERI-certified crackers authorised by PESO and carrying QR codes were permitted during specified morning and evening slots, for a total of three hours each day. From Nov 9, the use of all firecrackers was completely banned.In 2016, when there were no restrictions on bursting crackers, the AQI rose from 337 before Diwali to 431 on the festival day and peaked at 445 the following day.An analysis of 10 years of data shows that firecracker restrictions have been routinely flouted, while meteorological conditions have played a crucial role in determining pollution levels by influencing the dispersal of pollutants.This year, stronger winds initially helped disperse pollutants, but wind speeds slowed towards noon on Monday, reducing the atmosphere’s ability to disperse accumulated pollution. Lower wind speeds can cause pollutants to build up, particularly when emissions from traffic, construction and other urban sources continue. Atmospheric mixing and emissions from multiple sources also influence air quality.Station-level readings from Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) show that TERI Gram recorded the worst AQI at 405 (severe) post-Diwali, followed by NISE Gwal Pahari at 339, Vikas Sadan at 319 and Sector 51 at 289. TERI Gram also recorded the worst average PM2.5 concentration at 405 micrograms per cubic meter over the past 24 hours, with a maximum touching 500. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 311 micrograms per cubic meter.NISE Gwal Pahari recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 339 micrograms per cubic meter and PM10 of 252 micrograms per cubic meter. Vikas Sadan recorded an average of 319 micrograms per cubic meter for PM2.5 and 249 for PM10. Sector 51 recorded the best AQI at 289, with average PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations of 289 and 203 micrograms per cubic meter, respectively.“The wind speed was better yesterday, which helped disperse pollutants. As a result, the AQI improved on Diwali day, but the impact might not last long,” said Dipankar Saha, former head of the air laboratory at Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) air analyst Manoj Kumar said even short-term exposure to very high levels of air pollution can have adverse health effects. “Breathing polluted air can irritate the respiratory tract, aggravate existing conditions and increase the risk of respiratory symptoms. Children, the elderly and people with pre-existing health conditions, particularly those with respiratory or cardiovascular diseases, are more vulnerable because their bodies may be less equipped to cope with the additional stress. During periods of severe pollution, everyone should minimise prolonged outdoor exposure, especially strenuous physical activity, and take precautions to protect vulnerable individuals,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: 3 quick takeaways from the 49ers win over the Raiders: It was a day for the youngsters
articles.summary: The 49ers dominated on both sides of the ball on Sunday.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers blew by the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on Sunday, dominating the turnover battle while compiling over 400 total yards of offense.

The 49ers got off to a fast start and never looked back, though the win was overshadowed by a late, season-ending injury to defensive tackle Gracen Halton, who suffered a broken ankle.

Here are three quick takeaways from the 49ers win on Sunday.

The 49ers had a weird end-of-half scenario at the end of the second quarter. Getting a chance to get the ball back with just under two minutes left up 21-7, Kyle Shanahan let the clock run down 40 seconds with his two timeouts as Las Vegas kicked a field goal.

Then, after a first-down sack, the 49ers let the clock run out and didn't capitalize on a clear opportunity to score.

However, coming out of the half, Jaden Dugger got a pick-six on the first play from scrimmage, and suddenly, the score was 28-10. That was one of five second-half turnovers for the Raiders.

Las Vegas turned it over on four straight possessions, with a fumble, fumble, interception, and interception, taking away four scoring chances as the lead grew to 38-10. Initially, Fred Warner punched out a ball on Brock Bowers in 49ers territory, forcing the first turnover after the 49ers had an interception themselves.

Then San Francisco turned it over on downs, giving the Raiders another short field, but Michael Mayer fumbled on a big catch-and-run, losing the ball as he stretched for a touchdown and forcing a touchback.

After a seven-play, 80-yard touchdown drive for the 49ers to make it 35-17, the Raiders once again got down the field into the red zone, but Renardo Green picked off a pass in the red zone for another touchback.

This time, the 49ers drove down for a 12-play field goal drive to seal the deal at 38-17. Lastly, Malik Mustapha ended the game with another interception.

It was just a mean streak from the defense, as they racked up five turnovers on Sunday.

With the 49ers offense in its current state, San Francisco was going to have to rely on some of its younger players, just as it had to in the Atlanta Falcons game before the bye week. This time, the results were different.

Kaelon Black led the team in rushing with 70 yards on 11 carries, breaking off a couple of runs on the ground. In the air, Jordan Watkins made a couple of nice catches, leading the team with four catches for 86 yards, including a big 37-yard touchdown catch.

Defensively, Jaden Dugger, whose role has continued to grow, had six tackles, good for second on the team, a pass breakup, and his pick-six that really flipped the game for the 49ers.

It was a very good day for the young 49ers, and the team needed those big performances.

While the Raiders were busy turning the ball over, the 49ers dominated the time of possession 38:18 to 21:42 thanks to a number of well-executed long scoring drives.

The 49ers started fast, and that proved to be a huge boost, as they forced the Raiders to abandon the run, setting up the five second-half turnovers. San Francisco scored touchdowns on each of their first three drives, leading to a 21-10 halftime lead.

More importantly, San Francisco had a 12-play, 13-play, and 12-play drive over those three possessions, taking up nearly 20 minutes of clock.

Then, in the second half, the 49ers followed that up with drives of seven plays (for 80 yards) and 12 plays (for 63 yards) to end the game. It was a methodical day for the 49ers offense, and they executed well to sustain drives, dominating the time of possession while doing so.

articles.title: Tom Brady’s Former Babysitter Is the Mom of a Current Green Bay Packers Player
articles.summary: Tom Brady spotted his former babysitter in the most unlikely of places — the stands of a New England Patriots game against the Green Bay Packers, cheering on...
articles.body:
Tom Brady spotted his former babysitter in the most unlikely of places — the stands of a New England Patriots game against the Green Bay Packers , cheering on her son.

While providing color commentary for FOX Sports alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt during the Sunday, November 8, game between the two teams in Foxborough, Massachusetts, Burkhardt shared a surprising story about the former Patriots quarterback and current Packers safety Evan Williams .

After pointing out Williams' mother, Dani Williams , in the stands, Burkhardt shared, "You want to hear a story which we learned? She babysat you when you were 5 years old!"

"And I don't get surprised very often, but I was shocked," Brady, 49, exclaimed. "Evan Williams grew up in the Bay Area, and his mom said that when I was five years old, she was babysitting me. I said, 'I hope I was good when she was babysitting.'"

He then quipped, "I think we should throw in an extra tip now for being a bad boy."

Brady grew up in San Mateo, California, where he attended and played football for Junípero Serra High School. Williams, 25, meanwhile, went to high school at St. Francis in nearby Mountain View, California.

According to the seven-time Super Bowl champ, the two schools were "rivals," with Brady saying he asked Williams about his own record against Junípero Serra before the game.

"He said, 'I got a story for you, my mom used to babysit you,' and I was like, I'm never surprised, I was like, 'What do you mean?!'" Brady continued.

The two spoke with each other during a postgame interview as well, with the retired football star joking to Williams, "I'm going to get a hold of you and I'm going to figure out if I was a good kid or not, OK?"

"Yeah, we're gonna see because I heard no stories, which might be a bad thing!" Williams responded, as Brady awarded him the "LFG" ball for being the game's standout player.

The interview ended with Brady telling Williams to give his mother the ball as a present. "Send it my way and let's autograph it and we'll both give it to her," he added, "Job well done, my man, congratulations."

articles.title: Why Dan Orlovsky wants Vikings to make ‘outrageous’ trade calls for a QB
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings are 6-1 going into the “Monday Night Football” showdown against the Buffalo Bills. While it’s been a great start for the franchise, Min...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are 6-1 going into the " Monday Night Football " showdown against the Buffalo Bills. While it's been a great start for the franchise, Minnesota's success is largely supported by the defense. Offensively, things are just not clicking, as the quarterback situation is looking grim. Hours before kickoff, ESPN's Dan Orlovsky explained why he thinks the front office should be making trade calls before the deadline.

Carson Wentz will get the start after the Vikings opted to soft-bench Kyler Murray . It's a trial run to see if the 33-year-old can serve as the starting quarterback for the rest of the season. However, if things don't pan out against the Bills, Orlovsky believes the franchise must make "outrageous" trade calls to find a quarterback. He explained his reasoning while guest appearing on "The Pat McAfee Show."

"I want to see what the offense for Minnesota looks like tonight in relation to what it has for the majority of this season," Orlovsky said… "If this offense looks pedestrian again, I just do not believe Minnesota can stand pat. I think anything is on the table at quarterback. And when I say anything, I quite literally mean anything.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Even if it sounds outrageous to the NFL community," Orlovsky continued. "I think you have to start at, like, the most outrageous call you could make [for a] quarterback, and just work your way down the line. The most outrageous call you could make. However fantasy-stupid it sounds."

Wentz has made two appearances this season with one start. In those two games, the 11-year veteran has totaled 276 passing yards and three touchdowns while completing 59.0% of his pass attempts. All three of his touchdowns came in the 39-22 Week 1 win over the Green Bay Packers. Wentz stepped in for Murray early in the first quarter after Murray was knocked out of the contest with a concussion.

articles.title: Rhamondre Stevenson set to miss time with knee injury
articles.summary: The Patriots running back exited Sunday’s game in the third quarter.
articles.body:
The injuries continue to pile up for the New England Patriots, who now are set to be without another key offensive contributor for multiple weeks.

Running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added the injury is to the back of Stevenson's knee and is expected to keep him out the next few weeks.

Stevenson suffered the injury late in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers after being brought down following a six-yard reception. He was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game.

The back has been one of New England's most dependable players this season, playing 65% of the team's offensive snaps. Stevenson has totaled 399 yards and two touchdowns on 102 carries while adding 26 receptions for 258 yards and two touchdowns through the air. His contributions in pass protection have also earned consistent praise from head coach Mike Vrabel and his teammates.

With Stevenson and No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined, the Patriots are down to Corey Kiner and Lan Larison as their only running backs on the active roster ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Detroit Lions in Germany.

Kiner has seen the biggest workload in Henderson's recent absence, carrying the ball 50 total times this season for 244 yards and a touchdown.

"I think Corey is working extremely hard. I think Corey has done a really nice job," Vrabel said Monday. "But there are also some things that Corey has to be able to improve on, just like a lot of guys, as far as recognition of the pressure and then the ability to block the pressure that we saw yesterday, for example."

The Patriots also have running back Terrell Jennings on the practice squad.

articles.title: LIV Golf: What next for Bryson DeChambeau? How YouTube star can boost major hopes with return to traditional men's tours
articles.summary: On the latest Sky Sports Golf podcast, Paul McGinley discussed Bryson DeChambeau's  next career steps, the challenge welcoming LIV Golf players onto the DP World Tour and how the men's game could look going forward
articles.body:
DeChambeau's competitive future remains uncertain, following the demise of LIV Golf, with no pathway currently in place for an immediate return to the PGA Tour and no confirmation of how frequently he plans to tee it up in 2027.

The two-time major champion said in a statement on Sunday that he 'still believes in team golf', with the two-time US Open champion pledging to approach the next part of his career "with humility and respect."

He previous said he would focus on YouTube golf and "play tournaments that want him" if LIV Golf didn't survive, then recently revealed on the "Figuring Out" podcast that he hoped it 'exists forever' before the league entered the liquidation phase of bankruptcy.

On the possibility of YouTube golf becoming DeChambeau's focus going forward, McGinley told the Sky Sports Golf podcast: "You never know with Bryson, but I can see it. It would be a dumb move, to go from playing YouTube golf to trying to compete in majors.

"The longer Bryson stays away and off traditional platforms, the less chance he has of winning major championships going forward, because you cut your teeth in week-to-week PGA Tour and DP World Tour events before you elevate into these major championships.

"If you're cutting your teeth playing fun golf and LIV golf, it's a massive step up to then try and compete at the very top against the best players in the world - it's just not going to happen.

"You're training and preparing to win major championships at such a low level that you cannot step up in that way. If he does it [sticks with YouTube and team golf], I think it would pretty much close the door on him winning major championships during that period of time.

"If he comes back and plays the DP World Tour or the PGA Tour in the years to come, I think he could become a factor again winning majors, but not from LIV 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 and not even from YouTube golf."

DeChambeau was one of only two players to win a major while an active LIV Golf player, snatching the 2024 US Open before posting three top-10s in majors the following year, then missed the cut in the first three majors of 2026 as uncertainty grew over LIV Golf's future.

"With these guys who went to LIV, in the first couple of years they went, they were pretty competitive when it came to playing majors," McGinley explained. "The longer they stayed on LIV, the more disconnected they got from the top of the leaderboards in these majors.

"When Jon Rahm went to LIV, he was best player that Europe had in Italy in the Ryder Cup, the current Masters champion and one of the world's best. He went from that position to becoming a non-event when it comes to major championships.

"If you took money out of the equation and it was the same on LIV as it was on the PGA Tour and DP World Tour. If you said to each player 'which platform is going to give you the best opportunity to win major championships?', none of them would pick LIV.

"The reason they picked LIV and went on LIV was purely for financial reasons - it was not the ideal platform to prepare to win major championships."

DeChambeau is eligible to apply for DP World Tour membership for the 2027 season based on being a recent major champion, although has a November 15 deadline to confirm his position.

Sergio Garcia is among those to have their intention to return to the European circuit next year, having previously criticised the tour, with many DP World Tour players unhappy with the decision to welcome LIV Golf players back.

"Are all of these people coming back going to put 50 per cent back into the value of the tour in terms of the business model? Are sponsors suddenly going to be crawling over themselves to get involved with the DP World Tour? I don't think so," McGinley admitted.

"I'm not saying it's not great to have all the players back, but what is the end game here? The end game here is that the DP World Tour becomes more sustainable than already has been.

"Guy Kinnings [DP World Tour chief executive] will be in a very strong position in terms of where he gives these invites to, especially the guys who are not exempt and are trying to come back on the DP World Tour.

"He's got this balancing act of, yes, these guys from LIV do add somewhat of a value, but more importantly, he's got to firstly look after the guys who have played the DP World Tour for the last three, four, five years and who have remained loyal to that tour.

"There's also the young kids who have come through the HotelPlanner Tour, as well as DP World Tour's Q-school in the last couple of years, who have just got their status on the tour - they've got to be given real ample opportunity as well.

"Just because the big guys have come back to play, it can't be at their costs, so he's got this balancing act that he's going on. He understands as a member's organisation, he's got to be fair to the guys who stayed loyal, as well as the LIV guys coming back."

The Financial Times reported that BC Partners were reviving efforts to create a LIV Golf successor, suggesting they plan to acquire the PIF's bankruptcy loan to revive the league's assets.

" I think it [LIV Golf] is certainly in the dying embers - I wouldn't say it's 101 per cent gone," McGinley insisted. "There's a few rumours going round that LIV 3.0 might emerge, so let's just wait and see what happens.

"I think, to be honest, from a financial point of view, it was a nonsense anyway when it comes to a business model. I know that business quite well, obviously, from being on the DP World Tour board and I know the financials of world golf.

"I know the American business model is a very different ecosystem from the rest of the world. What they were trying to do, and the money they were putting on the table, it's very, hard - if not impossible - to get that kind of investment back."

McGinley added: "With all that's happened and people saying stuff and then doing something opposite that we've seen the last four years, I don't trust anybody and I don't trust anything that's come out.

"We've already been bitten by them saying one thing and doing another in the past. That's why I'm refusing to say that LIV 3.0 is not going to happen until November 15, when that line in the sand comes down from the DP World Tour."

articles.title: Charity take steps to challenge Northamptonshire solar farm
articles.summary: The government approves of the development Green Hill Solar Farm despite local opposition.
articles.body:
A countryside charity said it has taken steps towards challenging the government's recent decision to approve a solar farm scheme.

Last month the government approved the development of the Green Hill Solar Farm, which will be built over 2,965 acres (1,200 hectares) of land covering Buckinghamshire, the south and west of Wellingborough and north of Northampton.

The Campaign to Protect Rural England (CPRE) Northamptonshire said it had instigated a pre-action protocol letter for a judicial review to challenge the decision.

Island Green Power, the developer behind Green Hill Solar Farm, said: "As we have not yet received the pre-action protocol letter, we are unable to comment at this point.

"We will provide a formal response through the appropriate process once the formal letter has been reviewed."

In a statement posted on social media, CPRE Northamptonshire said: "Bad decisions such as this scheme cannot go unchallenged if the balance between renewable energy and food security is to be maintained."

The two Conservative MPs Sarah Bool, who represents South Northamptonshire, and Stuart Andrew, who represents Daventry, wrote to both West Northamptonshire Council and North Northamptonshire Council to ask if they were considering requesting a judicial review of the government's decision.

Bool said: "This was always the wrong application in the wrong place. A judicial review is the final line of defence and we want to make sure no stone is left unturned."

Andrew said: "I have opposed this development from the outset, and I won't stop standing up for the residents who have fought so hard against these plans."

In response Martin Griffiths, the Reform UK leader of North Northamptonshire Council, said he was examining the decision, adding: "The scale of this development has understandably caused considerable concern among residents, particularly about the impact on agricultural land, the countryside and the communities affected.

"We recognise that judicial review is concerned with the lawfulness of a decision rather than simply whether we agree with it.

"Any decision to proceed would need to be informed by appropriate legal advice and a proper assessment of the costs involved."

Green Hill Solar previously said it hoped construction would begin in 2027, with the aim of providing electricity to homes by 2029.

The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero said it could not comment on ongoing legal matters.
