articles.title: El juego lento, el mal que el golf quiere exterminar
articles.standfirst: El sector femenino ha tomado la delantera y castiga con dos golpes a los que se demoran mucho. En el masculino siguen siendo muy indulgentes
articles.summary: El sector femenino ha tomado la delantera y castiga con dos golpes a los que se demoran mucho. En el masculino siguen siendo muy indulgentes
articles.body: Hay pocas cosas que saquen más de quicio a un jugador de golf que compartir partido con alguien lento. Ese jugador que mira la bola, mira el hoyo, vuelve a mirar la bola, habla con el caddie, comprueba el viento, vuelve al libro, hace dos swings de prácticas, se coloca… se quita… vuelve a colocarse… y cuando por fin pega, los otros dos llevan un rato preguntándose “¿qué he hecho yo para merecer esto?”. Y si desespera al compañero de partido, imaginemos al espectador. El juego lento se ha convertido en un problemón para el golf. Y no hablamos solamente de educación o de cortesía entre jugadores. Hablamos de espectáculo. De televisión. De aficionados. De un deporte que pelea cada día por atraer nuevos públicos y que no puede permitirse que una vuelta dure cinco horas y media o seis. Casi una jornada laboral para completar 18 hoyos. No hay paciencia humana que aguante eso. Lo curioso es que el golf profesional tiene normas para combatirlo. El problema no es la ausencia de reglas. El problema es aplicarlas, especialmente cuando delante tienes a una estrella. Y ahí el golf femenino le está ganando la batalla a todos los demás porque no mira identidades. Hace apenas unas semanas, Carlota Ciganda estaba metida en la pelea por el Buick LPGA Shanghai cuando recibió dos golpes de penalización por juego lento. Su par en el hoyo 13 pasó a ser doble bogey. Dos golpes de una tacada. También Yealimi Noh, la número 44 del mundo, recibió otros dos aquel sábado. Se mira igual a la número 1 que a la 100. No era la primera vez para la navarra. En el Evian Championship de 2023 recibió otros dos golpes por juego lento. Recurrió la sanción y, al no incorporar finalmente esos dos golpes a su tarjeta, fue descalificada. Ya en 2021, en el LPGA Match Play, otra penalización por ritmo de juego en el hoyo 18 le había costado el partido ante Sarah Schmelzel. Desde el año pasado, la LPGA ha ido todavía más lejos. Si una jugadora supera entre seis y quince segundos el tiempo permitido, recibe un golpe; si se pasa 16 segundos o más, son dos. En 2025 Chisato Iwai recibió dos golpes en el Black Desert Championship y Yan Liu otros dos nada menos que en el Evian, un Major. A Im le cayó un golpe en el JM Eagle LA Championship y terminó perdiendo el torneo en playoff. Yubol recibió otro en el ShopRite LPGA Classic y acabó a un golpe de la victoria. Ahí es donde realmente duele una sanción: en la tarjeta, no en una multa que una profesional puede pagar y olvidar. No es un problema de género.También el golf masculino ha protagonizado jornadas insufribles. En el Open de 2025, en Royal Portrush, Rory McIlroy y Justin Thomas tardaron casi seis en completar su primera jornada. El problema es de todo el golf. La diferencia está en la diligencia empleada para solucionarlo. Marta Figueras-Dotti, presidenta del Ladies European Tour, comparte la preocupación y cree que el problema empieza mucho antes de llegar al profesionalismo. “Lo estamos viendo en los jóvenes, no solo en los profesionales sino en el golf en general", sostiene. 2Para mí, todas esas rutinas pre golpe y los 40 entrenadores que tiene cada uno han hecho mucho daño. Ahora hago la rutina, ahora pienso lo que me ha dicho el coach mental, ahora tomo esto porque me lo ha dicho el nutricionista… Y luego están las conversaciones con el caddie. No puede ser que se tarde seis horas en jugar”. La pionera española pone precisamente como ejemplo a Charley Hull o Linn Grant, jugadoras capaces de decidir rápido y jugar al máximo nivel sin eternizar cada golpe. “Hay demasiada información. Cuando te toca jugar ya tienes que estar preparada y haber tomado prácticamente la decisión antes de llegar a la bola. A los hombres les multan y les da igual pagar la multa. La medida que proponía Hull de quitar la tarjeta a la jugadora lenta. me parece muy drástica, pero creo que en el LET se han tomado medidas que están solucionando el problema. Ahora hay que enseñar a la gente a jugar rápido desde que empieza”. Porque el problema, evidentemente, no pertenece al golf femenino. David Howell, miembro del comité de torneos del DP World Tour, defendía recientemente que su circuito lleva años imponiendo multas y que los jugadores identificados habitualmente como lentos están sometidos a una vigilancia mucho mayor, aunque hasta Rory McIlroy ha elevado a la voz diciendo que no se sanciona con efectividad. "Es frustrante", dijo hace un año. Peor es al otro lado del Atlántico. En el PGA Tour las penalizaciones de golpes han sido históricamente excepcionales: la última en un torneo oficial del circuito se remonta a 2017. Mientras tanto, la discusión sobre el ritmo de juego reaparece temporada tras temporada. Alexandra Armas conoce bien el problema. Durante su etapa al frente del Ladies European Tour hizo del ritmo de juego una de las cuestiones a combatir y recuerda que no afectaba únicamente a las jugadoras. “Era un tema recurrente y problemático, no solo por la frustración que generaba entre las propias jugadoras, sino también por su impacto en la organización de los torneos y las retransmisiones televisivas, entre otros aspectos”. El LET fue endureciendo las medidas año tras año junto a los directores de torneo y el Comité de Jugadoras. “Creo que finalmente se ha encontrado un sistema que está funcionando bien: las jugadoras lo entienden y lo aceptan, y ha contribuido de forma significativa a agilizar las vueltas”. Las reglas existen. Los relojes existen. Las sanciones existen. Solo falta que todos las apliquen por igual.

articles.summary: Rory McIlroy looking to match Colin Montgomerie's record of eight times topping the DP World Tour Order of Merit; Eugenio Chacarra around 500 points clear of McIlroy ahead of the season-ending DP World Tour Championship; watch live on Sky Sports from 7am Thursday
articles.body:
McIlroy has topped the DP World Tour's Order of Merit for the past four seasons but heads into the 2026 DP World Tour Championship, live on Sky Sports from 7am on Thursday, second in the standings, over 500 points behind former LIV Golf player Chacarra.

The world No 2 hopes his experience at Jumeirah Golf Estates - he has won the season-ending tournament three times and lost in a play-off to Ryder Cup team-mate Matthew Fitzpatrick last year - will give him the edge at an event where 2,000 points go to the winner.

McIlroy said during his media duties on Tuesday: "The last few years I played well much earlier in the year where I've maybe not had to play at my absolute best to get it done. This week's a little bit different.

"The course has evolved a little bit over the years. It's certainly a lot more penal off the tee this year. The rough is very, very thick. You get a lot of bad lies in the rough.

"I think when you come back to a golf course that you played a lot on and you've done well on, that always gives you a little bit of an advantage starting the week.

"I think there's a little bit there [in having experience of the course]."

On having the chance to emulate Montgomerie, McIlroy, who finished third at last week's Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, four strokes behind winner Jon Rahm, said: "I'm very excited to be in contention for the eighth. I made some ground up last week, maybe not as much as I wanted, but I felt like it was a step in the right direction.

"It's been a course that's been very good to me over the years, and I have a lot of experience on it and a lot of experience up at the top end of the leaderboard.

"I'm excited to do it all over again, to try to play well enough to give myself a real chance at the weekend."

McIlroy completed the career Grand Slam in 2025 after finally claiming an elusive Masters title - 11 years after his previous major triumph - and then made it back-to-back victories at Augusta National in April of this year.

The 37-year-old told reporters he is "increasingly proud" of his "consistency" and "longevity" over the years as he targets what would be a 45th career title should he win the DP World Tour Championship in the Emirates this week.

McIlroy added: "I think this will be the 15th or 16th year in a row that I will have finished the year in the top 10 in the world rankings.

"I think maybe an underrated part of careers is that longevity piece.

"I've stayed pretty much injury-free and I've kept working and trying to get better at certain aspects of the game, always tried to see weaknesses or be critical of myself and try to get better at them.

"That approach has worked really well for me and hopefully will continue to work well for me for a few more years yet."

Rahm: Chacarra has a game that works on every course

Rahm, who sits sixth in the standings after his success in Abu Dhabi and has a chance of a second Race to Dubai title, after 2019 , said of current leader, and fellow Spaniard, Chacarra: "Not much can be said about his golf game that isn't already known.

"He's a phenomenal ball-striker, has a great ball flight and the type of game that works on every golf course on the planet, stable in any condition.

"If the putter is at an average level, he's always going to have a chance and mentally you can tell he's somebody that wants to be there.

"When it's a Sunday and he gets close, he is not usually a name that falls off. He stays there, puts the pressure on.

"He's brave enough to do that and has a lot of confidence in himself, which you need."

Watch all four rounds of the DP World Tour Championship live on Sky Sports. Coverage of the opening round gets under way from 7am on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event on Thursday. Get the latest Sky Sports deals or stream contract-free .

articles.title: Bryson DeChambeau: American running out of options after LIV Golf collapse, says Rory McIlroy
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy says the addition of Bryson DeChambeau to the DP World Tour next season would bring more "eyeballs" to the tour but feels the American is running out of options.
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy says the addition of Bryson DeChambeau to the DP World Tour next season would bring more "eyeballs" to the tour but feels the American is running out of options.

DeChambeau's competitive future is uncertain following the collapse of LIV Golf , with the two-time US Open champion last week saying he will approach his next move with "humility and respect".

The 33-year-old American can apply for DP World Tour membership based on his status as a recent major champion, which would offer him the chance to earn back his PGA Tour card for 2028.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," said McIlroy, who was pipped to the 2024 US Open in dramatic fashion by DeChambeau.

"Honestly, I'm certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be but it doesn't seem like he's got many options.

"You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn't seem like he's got many options."

I'm not going to rewrite last four years - DeChambeau on LIV

LIV confirms intention to wind down after five years

LIV aimed to 'destroy the European Tour' - McIlroy

Northern Ireland's McIlroy was speaking to reporters in Dubai before the DP World Tour Championship as he chases a record-equalling eighth season-long title.

The six-time major winner trails Spain's Eugenio Chacarra by 533 points in the Race to Dubai standings going into the final event in Dubai, which offers 2,000 points to the winner.

Nine players - Chacarra, McIlroy, Patrick Reed, Casey Jarvis, Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier - can still clinch the Race to Dubai title, but McIlroy would guarantee his fifth straight crown with victory at Jumeirah Golf Estates this week.

McIlroy's excellent record at the Dubai tournament includes three wins and a play-off defeat by England's Matt Fitzpatrick last year.

"I'm very excited to be back here, very excited to be in contention for the eighth," said the 37-year-old.

"I made some ground up last week, maybe not as much as I wanted, but I felt like it was a step in the right direction.

"Getting back to a place where I played, I played well and I had a lot of success, even last year in the play-off with Matt, it's been a course that's been very good to me over the years, and I have a lot of experience on it and a lot of experience up at the top end of the leaderboard."

An eighth Race to Dubai title would draw McIlroy alongside Colin Montgomerie, who won seven straight European Tour Order of Merit titles in the 1990s before adding an eighth in 2005.

With McIlroy chasing a fifth successive Race to Dubai title, he spoke about how proud he is of the "consistency" and "longevity" he has shown in his career.

"I think this will be the 15th or 16th year in a row that I will have finished the year in the top 10 in the world rankings," said the world number two.

"There may be a couple others that have done that before. Yeah, I'm very proud of that. I think that's maybe an underrated part of careers, is that longevity piece.

"I was very lucky to start so young and get my tour card at 18, and I've stayed pretty much injury-free throughout my career.

"And I've kept working and trying to get better at certain aspects of the game and always tried to see weaknesses or be critical of myself and try to get better at them."

articles.title: DP World Tour: English golfer Frank Kennedy denies 'deliberate damage' after being disqualified from Q-School
articles.summary: Frank Kennedy says he did not intentionally damage green after swinging putter in frustration after missing a birdie putt; Englishman was removed from DP World Tour Q-School with organisers noting "serious misconduct"; Kennedy won on the HotelPlanner Tour as an 18-year-old in 2024
articles.body:
The 21-year-old from Manchester was tied for 28th after 72 holes of a 108-hole event at which the top 15 and ties earn a DP World Tour card.

He was removed for what organisers called "serious misconduct".

Kennedy issued a statement on Instagram which read: "I did not intentionally or deliberately damage the putting surface, and any comments saying otherwise are wholly incorrect.

"On the 11th green I missed a birdie putt and tapped in. In frustration, as I was walking off the green, I swung my putter and it accidentally caught the surface.

"My playing partner and I repaired it straight away, and we were both satisfied it was properly fixed before we moved on. I should have called a referee to check the repair, and I've learned from that.

"I have always respected and followed the rules of golf. If accidental contact like this, repaired at once, is a disqualification offence, I will respect that.

"But it isn't clear to me that it is, and many senior players I've spoken to this evening were surprised by the decision.

"So, I have asked the DP World Tour for clarification and a review, and I will respect the outcome of that review. While that happens, I won't be commenting further."

Kennedy, currently ranked 777th in the world, won an event on the HotelPlanner Tour, the tier below the DP World Tour, as an 18-year-old in 2024, triumphing at the Euram Bank Open in Austria.

articles.title: Rahm: "Hay que dejar de culpar a LIV de mi mal juego en los 'majors'"
articles.standfirst: El jugador analizó su rendimiento en la mayoría de los 'grandes' de los tres últimos años antes de que arranque la final del DP World Tour
articles.summary: El jugador analizó su rendimiento en la mayoría de los 'grandes' de los tres últimos años antes de que arranque la final del DP World Tour
articles.body: El golfista español Jon Rahm aseguró este martes que su mal rendimiento en la mayoría de los 'majors' en los tres últimos años, coincidiendo con su etapa en LIV, se debió a su "mal juego", no al hecho de haber militado en la liga saudí, de la que se desvinculó hace pocas semanas antes del anuncio de su liquidación. "Hay que dejar de culpar a LIV por mi mal juego en los 'majors'. Es lo que todos intentan insinuar. No es por culpa de LIV. Es culpa mía. Porque tuve la oportunidad de ganar el Campeonato d la PGA los dos últimos años que lo jugamos, ¿verdad? Es mi responsabilidad y, digamos, mis problemas con el 'swing'", explicó Rahm. El jugador vasco ofreció una rueda de prensa en el campo Jumeirah Golf Estates de Dubái, donde este jueves comienza la final del DP World Tour después de su triunfo el pasado domingo en Abu Dabi, su primera victoria desde que dejó LIV. En caso de repetir victoria en Dubái y si sus rivales no obtienen un buen resultado, Rahm tiene opciones de proclamarse mejor jugador del año del circuito europeo, la llamada 'Race to Dubai', algo que ya consiguió en 2019. "Significaría muchísimo. Creo que sería un paso más para, con suerte, acercarme a lo que Seve (Ballesteros) logró. Pero aún queda mucho camino por recorrer (...) Sería especial. De no saber que tenía una oportunidad, a llegar en las últimas dos semanas y lograrlo", comentó el exnúmero uno del mundo sobre la posibilidad de coronarse y aproximarse a los seis títulos de la orden de mérito europea que logró la gran leyenda del golf español. Rahm es sexto en la clasificación del circuito, que lidera el español Eugenio Chacarra, por delante del norirlandés Rory McIlroy. Preguntado por su balance de la temporada, el 'León de Barrika' respondió: "He jugado muy bien este año. Lo que pasa es que, por desgracia, algunas de mis peores semanas han coincidido con los 'majors'. Aparte del Campeonato de la PGA, donde tuve buenas posibilidades de ganar, en los otros tres 'majors' no rendí lo suficiente". "En general, muy bien, pero esos torneos son tan importantes para todos que me arrepiento un poco", se sinceró el jugador vasco, que en su etapa en LIV ganó cuatro torneos, pero ninguno fuera de ese circuito, aunque en el último Campeonato de la PGA fue segundo. Rahm lo achacó a que en los torneos regulares "es más fácil compensar algunos fallos técnicos y cuando la presión es máxima y el escenario es el más grande, es cuando esos errores se acentúan". El jugador vizcaíno abogó por que el golf también tenga un Mundial por selecciones como hay en la mayoría de las disciplinas: "Hay muy pocos deportes en el mundo que no tengan una Copa Mundial, y el golf es uno de ellos. Si hubiera una manera de hacer algo así, creo que lo recibiría con los brazos abiertos. Sería muy divertido".

articles.title: “Hopefully He Gets Traded to an Actual NBA Team” – Fans React to Anthony Davis’ Monster 44-Point Double-Double in Blowout Loss to Pistons
articles.summary: Anthony Davis continued to dominate on Monday with a 44-point double-double, grabbing 13 rebounds and shooting 76. 2% from the field (2-for-4 from 3) against...
articles.body:
Anthony Davis continued to dominate on Monday with a 44-point double-double, grabbing 13 rebounds and shooting 76.2% from the field (2-for-4 from 3) against the Detroit Pistons. However, the Washington Wizards lost their fourth straight game, dropping to 4-7, as Detroit won 122-111.

The Wizards seem to have exceptionally talented players around Davis in the starting lineup, but their bench has been underwhelming. They aren't deep enough to beat contending teams. They still haven't beaten a team over .500. The Wizards losing despite Davis' best game of the season has raised concerns about their playoff aspirations.

It also wasn't the first time they've lost a game where he's played well. With Davis playing at his peak amid Washington's struggles, several fans pushed to see him on a contending team after Monday's performance.

"Hopefully he gets traded to an actual NBA team at some point," one fan said.

Theo Pinson urges Warriors to trade for Anthony Davis

Former Dallas Mavericks player Theo Pinson has urged the Warriors to trade for Anthony Davis. Rumors linked the Warriors and Davis all summer, as it was considered a package deal if LeBron James chose Golden State in free agency. However, James headed to Philadelphia and Davis stayed put in Washington.

On Monday, Pinson made a compelling case for the Warriors to pursue Davis again on "The Baha" podcast. Pinson said the Warriors should part with Jimmy Butler to make the deal happen and give Steph Curry a better chance of contending in the playoffs.

"If you want to make the best out of your Steph Curry, Draymond Green situation, do you have a better chance of winning a championship with Jimmy Butler and this team orchestrated? Or Anthony Davis? I would take the chance with Anthony Davis," Pinson said. "That's a better risk to me. And no one can discredit what Jimmy Butler has done in the playoffs, but he is coming off an ACL injury and that is a fact. But a seven-foot near guard who can play on both ends of the floor- I'm taking a chance on that."

"If you want to make the best out of your Steph Curry, Draymond Green situation, do you have a better chance of winning a championship with Jimmy Butler and this team orchestrated? Or Anthony Davis? I would take the chance with Anthony Davis," Pinson said.

"That's a better risk to me. And no one can discredit what Jimmy Butler has done in the playoffs, but he is coming off an ACL injury and that is a fact. But a seven-foot near guard who can play on both ends of the floor- I'm taking a chance on that."

The Warriors started 0-3 but have turned things around with an eight-game winning streak. Curry is playing at an MVP-caliber level, averaging 30.6 points and 4.3 assists, shooting 50.3% from the field and 45.7% from 3.

Curry and the Warriors are thriving despite missing three huge pieces: Jimmy Butler, Kristaps Porzingis, and Moses Moody. Adding a force like Anthony Davis could elevate them to a whole new level, giving them the rim protection and paint presence they've lacked for years.

If Butler had been healthy, Davis might not have been on Golden State's radar. However, Butler is coming off an ACL surgery at 37 and can shake things up. While Davis has been injury-prone over the past couple of years, he's still played like a top-five center when healthy and would likely have more impact than Butler at this stage.

articles.title: ‘Firecrackers unfairly blamed for Delhi pollution’: CTI cites high pre-Diwali AQI, seeks action on stubble burning
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Firecracker sales in Delhi were estimated at around Rs 300 crore this Diwali, Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Firecracker sales in Delhi were estimated at around Rs 300 crore this Diwali, Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said on Tuesday.He argued that firecrackers were being unfairly held responsible for the national capital's pollution, urging political parties to join hands to tackle stubble burning and other sources of pollution.Speaking about the Diwali business, Goyal said Delhi continued to be a major market for firecrackers, most of which are sourced from Sivakasi and other places.He said businesses could have managed sales better if permissions had been granted earlier."Firecracker sales were good this Diwali, with business estimated at around Rs 300 crore. Delhi is a major market, although most firecrackers come from Sivakasi and other places. Earlier permission would have helped businesses manage sales better," he said.Goyal argued that although firecrackers generate some smoke, their impact is temporary and other pollution sources also need to be tackled."Firecrackers are being unfairly blamed for Delhi's pollution. While they do cause some smoke, their impact is temporary. Pollution levels are already high between October and January, even before Diwali, so stubble burning and other sources must also be addressed," he added.In a letter dated November 10 to political parties, CTI said it was against pollution but opposed holding Diwali firecrackers solely responsible for the city's poor air quality.It urged political parties to work with the Central government to find solutions to stubble burning in their respective states.The trade body questioned why Delhi's pollution levels were high even before Diwali, pointing out that the air quality index (AQI) stood between 350 and 400 on November 5, 6 and 7, while firecrackers were burst on November 8."That pollution was caused by whom? No firecrackers were burst at that time," the letter said, contending that the figures showed firecrackers were not the only source of pollution in Delhi.CTI also flagged the recurring deterioration in air quality between October and January, attributing it partly to stubble burning in neighbouring states. It urged political parties to concentrate on resolving the issue instead of targeting firecracker traders.Highlighting the economic consequences of restrictions on the trade, CTI claimed that around 10 lakh people across the country were associated with the firecracker industry, from manufacturers in Sivakasi to small retailers in Delhi.It said many small traders invest throughout the year and rely on the 15-20 days around Diwali to earn their annual income.The organisation further said traders had invested in licensed stocks and green firecrackers, arguing that restrictions imposed at the last minute affected their investments and livelihoods.CTI suggested a middle path that would allow fewer firecrackers, limit their use to designated timings and encourage green firecrackers instead of imposing a complete ban. It also expressed concern over the impact of restrictions on children's festival celebrations.The letter also questioned what it described as selective restrictions on Hindu festivals in the name of environmental protection, referring to Diwali, Holi, Chhath, Kanwar Yatra and Ganesh visarjan. It called for laws to be enforced equally across all festivals and occasions.Asking political parties to guarantee that Delhi's AQI would not exceed 300 between October and January if firecrackers were completely banned, CTI said the answer lay in scientific and balanced pollution management throughout the year."We want clean air, businesses to continue, traditions to be preserved, children's happiness to remain and the law to be equal for everyone," the letter stated.The letter was signed by CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal and other office-bearers of the organisation.(With inputs from ANI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Rory McIlroy Talks Bryson DeChambeau's Future in Video, 'Doesn't Seem Like He's Got Many Options'
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy doesn't think Bryson DeChambeau has many choices outside of accepting what is reportedly a chance to play on the DP World Tour.
articles.body:
Rory McIlroy doesn't think Bryson DeChambeau has many choices outside of accepting what is reportedly a chance to play on the DP World Tour.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau, and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," McIlroy said Tuesday ahead of Thursday's start of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

"And honestly, look— I'm certainly not in his shoes, nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn't seem like he's got many options if he wants to play competitive golf."

DeChambeau left the PGA Tour in 2022 to join LIV Golf, which confirmed last week it is ending operations among ongoing bankruptcy court proceedings.

"Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," DeChambeau wrote in a statement shared last week. "Whatever comes next, I'II approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before."

The Telegraph 's James Corrigan reported last week DeChambeau had been offered "full playing privileges on the European circuit next year."

"The 23-year-old is the only Tour non-member on LIV who has this exemption and if he decides to enlist for 2027 he could earn back his PGA Tour card for 2028 via the Race to Dubai money list," Corrigan reported.

Eligibility criteria for the PGA Tour as of September dictates a one-year suspension for players participating in LIV Golf dating back to their last tournament. That would keep players including DeChambeau away from the PGA Tour until at least August 2027.

The PGA Tour previously opened a direct path for LIV Golf players including DeChambeau under the Returning Member Program, through which Brooks Koepka agreed to significant financial penalties to immediately rejoin the organization. Koepka forfeited an estimated $50 to $85 million in career earnings by agreeing to the program, per PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp .

Rolapp said in August the PGA Tour is not planning to reinstate a similar program.

Jon Rahm said last week he would accept similar conditions to get his own path back to the PGA Tour but would "seriously doubt I get offered the same deal that Brooks did," per the Golf Channel .

"It's a pretty good safety net that I have that I can play the DP World Tour next year, and if it comes to that, I'm really excited to play for a full year," Rahm said last week.

DeChambeau said in 2022 he was paid more than $125 million to join LIV Golf. He earned an estimated $68.7 million in winnings on the tour, per Spotrac .

Bankruptcy filings described by USA Today's Mark Giannotto and Kristie Ackert show LIV Golf acknowledging $5.77 million still owed to DeChambeau.

DeChambeau confirmed in his statement he would be playing at the DP World Tour's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa this December and then "go about whatever is next the right way."

The Athletic's Gabby Herzig recently reported the PGA Tour "is not expected to make a public decision about a pathway back for LIV Golf players until at least January, when LIV's bankruptcy proceedings are set to conclude."

Whether PGA Tour ultimately considers reinstating another return pathway could shape whether DeChambeau ends up playing a full upcoming season with the DP World Tour.

articles.title: Golfer Disqualified From DP World Tour Q-School Tournament After Damaging Green With Club
articles.summary: The DP World Tour announced Tuesday that it upheld its decision to disqualify a golfer from a DP World Tour Qualifying School event for damaging a green.
articles.body:
The DP World Tour announced Tuesday that it upheld its decision to disqualify a golfer from a DP World Tour Qualifying School event for damaging a green.

According to GolfMagic.com's Andy Roberts , 21-year-old British golfer Frank Kennedy was disqualified from the final stage of the DP World Tour Qualifying School tournament at Infinitum Golf Resort in Spain this week.

In a statement, the DP World Tour explained that the DQ was a result of Kennedy engaging in "serious misconduct after causing deliberate damage to the course."

Kennedy responded to the ruling in a post on Instagram , writing, "I am hugely disappointed to have been disqualified from the Final Stage of DP World Tour Qualifying School. Reports today say this was for deliberately damaging the course. I did not intentionally or deliberately damage the putting surface, and any comments saying otherwise are wholly incorrect."

He continued by noting that after missing a birdie putt on the par-five 11th hole, swung his putter and "accidentally caught the surface" of the green.

Kennedy wrote that he and his playing partner "repaired it straight away, and we were both satisfied it was properly fixed before we moved on."

However, Kennedy did admit that he "should have called the referee to check the repair."

Kennedy asked the DP World Tour to review its decision, and in a statement provided to Tod Leonard of Golf Digest , the tour stood by its ruling.

The statement read, "The ruling to disqualify him under Rule 1.2a of the Rules of Golf—made by the Qualifying School Rules Committee for serious misconduct for damaging the 11th green during the fourth round—stands."

Kennedy—who won the Euram Bank Open on the Challenge Tour in 2024—had been vying to earn his DP World Tour card, but the disqualification knocked him out of contention.

articles.title: Jon Rahm Says 'We Gotta Stop Blaming LIV' Golf for His Struggles at Majors in Recent Years
articles.summary: With Jon Rahm's professional future unclear amid his recent departure from LIV Golf, the 32-year-old is not blaming the defunct circuit for his struggles at major tournaments.
articles.body:
With Jon Rahm's professional future unclear amid his recent departure from LIV Golf, the 32-year-old is not blaming the defunct circuit for his struggles at major tournaments.

Speaking to reporters ahead of this weekend's DP World Tour event, Rahm explained "we gotta stop blaming LIV" for the issues he has had in the four majors in recent years.

"It's not because of LIV. It's my own," Rahm said. "Because I did have a chance to win the PGA the last two years we played it, right. It's my own doing and my own, let's say, golf swing problems. That's what I was alluding, that when you are not playing a big event, it's a lot easier to manage certain things."

Rahm's run on the PGA Tour from 2021 to 2023 had him in the discussion for the best golfer in the world. He won the 2021 U.S. Open and 2023 Masters, along with three other top-five finishes in majors during that period.

After his victory at the 2023 Masters, Rahm moved back up to No. 1 in the Official World Golf Rankings. He announced at the end of the year he was signing a deal with LIV Golf reportedly worth between $450-600 million.

In the three seasons since his move, Rahm finished in the top 10 four times in 11 major appearances. He missed the 2024 U.S. Open due to a foot injury.

Rahm's best major finish during his LIV tenure was at in May at the PGA Championship when he tied for second, three shots behind Aaron Rai. He did win four LIV tournaments, including twice this year.

LIV announced last week plans to shut down after previously filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy due to losing financial backing. Rahm was released from his contract as part of a separation agreement filed in a New Jersey court last month.

Rahm is coming off a win at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship on the DP World Tour last weekend. It's unclear if he will return to the PGA Tour, though he has expressed a willingness to accept the same penalties Brooks Koepka received to get back on the circuit.

Koepka agreed to a five-year forfeiture of potential equity in the PGA Tour's Player Equity Program and a $5 million charitable donation as part of his conditions to return to the PGA Tour.

Rahm originally joined the PGA Tour in 2016 after wrapping up his college career at Arizona State. He won 11 tournaments on the circuit before joining LIV.

articles.title: LIV Golf Shuts Down: The End Of A Five-Year Experiment
articles.summary: LIV Golf closes its doors after five years. See what Bryson DeChambeau and Rory McIlroy say about the league's collapse and the future of the game.
articles.body:
LIV Golf officially closed up shop on November 5, marking the end of a five-year experiment funded by Saudi Arabia. The league launched with big promises and huge checks, but it could not sustain itself without its primary financial backer. This sudden halt leaves players scrambling for their next moves while the PGA Tour watches from the sidelines.

ESPN staff writer Paolo Uggetti shared the details on why the league shut down, noting that the financial support from the Public Investment Fund has dried up. Saudi Arabia's global sports influence shift was contextualized by Sarath Ganji, who founded the Autocracy and Global Sports Initiative, during this era. The money that once flowed freely to sign top talent is no longer available, forcing an orderly winding-down process.

The dream of a new era for professional golf died quickly once the funding stopped. Phil Mickelson proclaimed LIV would be a game changer that brought the PGA Tour to its knees, but that never happened. It was never destined to become the "force for change and good," that Bryson DeChambeau once mocked so laughably.

According to Lee News Central , LIV amounted to nothing beyond a cash grab. Because it was always amoral at its core and utterly devoid of principles, failure was inevitable like so many other things.

From the beginning, Rory McIlroy, who became golf's conscience through his fierce opposition to LIV, anticipated the conclusion. "I think that there is going to be a bit of a reset here, just for things to be a little bit more sustainable," McIlroy said on Wednesday, November 4, when it became clear LIV was circling the drain.

With the league gone, players are already looking for new ways to make money. While he had previously collaborated with the brand on headcovers, this new deal expands their relationship to feature his own dedicated clothing collection.

DeChambeau shared seven photographs announcing the news on social media alongside an enthusiastic message for his followers. "I'm excited for this one," he wrote. "Headcovers were just the start… now I'm expanding my partnership with @swaggolfco into apparel!"

The new collection drops November 19 online and in stores at Dick's Sporting Goods and Golf Galaxy. Despite the league ending, DeChambeau insisted he had no regrets about joining in the summer of 2022. "I'm not going to rewrite the last four years. I made a decision I believed in, and I'm grateful for what came with it," he wrote.

Some might argue the lack of a financial war is bad for players, but McIlroy disagrees. "There's not as much of an arms race as there was maybe a couple of years ago, and some players will argue that that's not good for players. I think that's very short-term thinking," McIlroy said. "If you want sustainable tours, and we want these tours around in 50 years' time, there has to be sustainable business practices in place to make sure they are."

articles.title: Tiger Woods Gives Injury Update, Confirms Next PGA Tour Event He'll Attend Amid Training
articles.summary: It remains to be seen when Tiger Woods will play in another PGA Tour event, but he will be in attendance at the Hero World Challenge from Dec. 3-6.
articles.body:
It remains to be seen when Tiger Woods will play in another PGA Tour event, but he will be in attendance at the Hero World Challenge from Dec. 3-6.

"I'm feeling better," the golf legend told SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio. "No doubt about that. I've been training quite a bit. I will be at Hero. I'm there either way, so I'll see you there."

Woods is the host of the tournament in the Bahamas, so his presence comes as anything but a surprise. He even laughed at the situation during the interview with SiriusXM since the question was surely aimed more at figuring out when he will be back on the course.

The 15-time major champion has not played in a PGA Tour tournament since the Open Championship in July 2024.

Injuries and a number of surgeries have been a significant issue for the all-time great in the latter portion of his career, although ESPN's Mark Schlabach reported last month he is expected to play for Jupiter Links Golf Club on Dec. 27 when the upcoming TGL season begins.

Woods played in just one match during the previous TGL season after he underwent another back surgery.

Fans may not have to wait that long to see him play, though, if he does take the course for the Hero World Challenge.

There is also the PNC Championship from Dec. 17-20, where he may play alongside his son Charlie and is allowed to use a cart. That is a 36-hole, two-person scramble tournament that isn't as physically taxing.

While there is still some uncertainty regarding when he will play again, golf fans can at least take solace knowing Woods is training and will be in attendance at the Hero World Challenge.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy knows Bryson DeChambeau, with limited options post-LIV Golf, would bring 'eyeballs' to DP World Tour
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy will play at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai this week.
articles.body:
While he may not be the biggest fan, Rory McIlroy knows Bryson DeChambeau would be a significant boost for the DP World Tour next season.

And, after LIV Golf's collapse, it may be DeChambeau's only option.

"I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments," McIlroy said on Tuesday ahead of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai. "And honestly, look, I'm certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn't seem like he's got many options. If he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn't seem like he's got many options."

"And honestly, look, I'm certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn't seem like he's got many options. If he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn't seem like he's got many options."

DeChambeau had been all-in on "LIV 2.0" in recent weeks, and even said on a podcast last month that he thought the new version of the league made "full financial sense" and could exist "forever."

But last week, LIV Golf officially moved to shut down after losing a funding plan from BC Partners. The league, which once caused so much chaos in the golf world , had been struggling to find a path forward after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced earlier this year that it would stop funding it.

DeChambeau has several paths forward, depending on what he wants to do. He announced on Sunday that he will play in the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa in December, but didn't reveal plans beyond that.

The DP World Tour has offered DeChambeau full status with its league in 2027, if he wants it. But DeChambeau has to commit by next week. If he goes that route, DeChambeau could spend the year in Europe while earning his PGA Tour card back, something Patrick Reed has been doing all season. Other former LIV Golf members, like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton, are planning to do that in 2027.

Or, DeChambeau could try to strike a deal with the PGA Tour to return early. Brooks Koepka received a deal in January through the "Returning Member's Program," but it cost him an estimated $85 million in earnings . It's unclear if that'll be offered again, or what it would look like.

DeChambeau has also said he could just keep doing his own thing and playing the major championships while growing his YouTube channel. That path wouldn't be sustainable long term, unless he keeps winning majors and earning exemptions into those tournaments.

Regardless, DeChambeau will have to make a decision soon.

"I don't really get any satisfaction from making a decision and watching the other guys have to sit out a year and have the repercussions of that," Reed said on Tuesday in Dubai. "The more satisfaction is going out there and playing solid golf. You never want to see guys struggle or have to sit out, things like that. I mean, we're all competitors. We're all athletes and really, at the end of the day, a lot of those guys that are going through that are good friends of mine. articles.title: LIV Golf Files Bankruptcy Plan and Sets Sight on January Liquidation
articles.summary: LIV Golf filed a Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan with a New Jersey court Tuesday, along with a proposed schedule for a final hearing on its disclosure statement on Jan. 7 that would begin liquidation.
articles.body:
LIV Golf filed a Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan with a New Jersey court Tuesday, along with a proposed schedule for a final hearing on its disclosure statement on Jan. 7 that would begin liquidation.

LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy on Sept. 8 after the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, which had bankrolled the breakaway league from the start, said a change in strategy meant it would no longer pay for LIV after the 2026 season.

The bankruptcy plan is for an orderly wind down of LIV. The restructuring agreement with BC Partners Credit, which had pledged $300 million, failed to garner enough support for a LIV 2.0 version that would have kept the league going in 2027.

"Debtors have determined that no viable restructuring transaction remains available due to lack of player participation and BC Partners' termination of the Restructuring Support Agreement," LIV said in a summary of the bankruptcy plan.

It said PIF invested approximately $5 billion in equity capital and that LIV Golf continually operated at a loss and was years away from profitability. The filing also revealed LIF laid off 289 employees and furloughed 22 others roughly a week before filing for bankruptcy.

This was about a month after it finished paying $15.6 million in retention bonuses to seven executives LIV said was essential to finishing the 2026 season and making plans for restructuring.

A hearing is scheduled for Nov. 24 to conditionally approve the disclosure statement, which requires adequate information for those to whom LIV owes money and begins the wind-down phase of LIV operations.

The six weeks in between the Jan. 7 hearing to approve the statement are to determine voting rights and take any objections from those who have claims. A wind-down trust would oversee payments to creditors, resolve legal claims and handle other financial matters.

The judge last week approved Jon Rahm's separation from LIV, which cost the two-time major champion a reported $100 million he was owed from when he joined the Saudi-funded league at the end of 2023. Rahm won last week in Abu Dhabi for his first regular European tour title since 2022.

The other LIV players, who have been banned by the PGA Tour, now must figure out where to play. Some have European tour membership or can try to get sponsor exemptions to tournaments, though not the strongest events on the schedule.

The PGA Tour has not indicated a path back for players and likely won't until the bankruptcy proceedings are over.

articles.title: Seminoles collapse in final minutes versus Florida, lose 81-72
articles.summary: At least the next five games are super easy…
articles.body:
Well, they gave them a scare in the first half.

Florida State (2-1, 0-0 ACC) played the No. 1 team in the nation, the Florida Gators (3-0, 0-0 SEC), and ultimately could not muster enough juice to take down their rivals. The Seminoles ultimately fell by nine in a game that saw eight lead changes.

The three-point department was miserable in the first half, 0-for-9 beyond the arc. Florida hit five out of eighteen. However, the Seminoles never let it go beyond a six-point Florida lead. FSU had six turnovers in the first half compared to Florida's seven.

With 0:39 left in the first half, Sebastian Rancik would hit a 12-footer to take the lead, 29-28, but Florida would hit a three thanks to Thomas Haugh to go into the locker room up 31-29.

Kam Taylor hit a nasty dunk after a loose ball was tipped by Alex Steen to put FSU within one point with 16 minutes to go, and he ended up finishing with 10 points and three assists.

Florida would take this down the stretch, with a lead of 10 and just four minutes to go, to which FSU responded essentially with a chess match, fouling. Unfortunately, Florida's free-throw shooters couldn't be stopped. They finished with 30/41 made shots, good for 73%, lower than FSU's 14/18, or 78%.

It was a game that saw limited action from the bench, with Steen, Schweiger, and Assui all scoring just two points. Steen and Assui were on the court for more than 15 minutes, with the former getting four rebounds and two steals. Assui managed two offensive and two defensive rebounds as well.

The Seminoles finished with an offensive rating of 105.9 and a defensive efficiency rating of 119.1. In a losing effort against the No. 1 team in the nation, it's admirable. FSU has now lost close twice in a row against the Gators. Finishing with fewer total turnovers than the Gators is also noteworthy, and several of them happened when they were in desperation mode, so I think this says more about Florida being more mortal than one thought.

Sebastian Rancik was responsible for 1/3 of the Seminoles' points with 23 in 32 minutes. He's averaging 22 points per game.

Florida State stays home and begins the easy part of their non-conference schedule with a match against Texas A&M Corpus Christi. Fans can catch that game on the ACC Network Extra. Then they welcome the Ball State Cardinals to town, followed by another home game against Green Bay.
